Hi Megan — thanks for the v3 and the clear list. Quick replies inline below, and I've attached a proposed payment construct (redlines_annotated.docx) that marries our finance needs with Hearthline's ask.

- Payment schedule: We can support a phased invoicing approach. Proposed: 30% invoice at execution (covers reserved capacity), 35% invoice at Month 3 post-activation, 35% at renewal/annual anniversary. - Net terms: Our standard Net terms for new enterprise pilots are Net 45. We can try Net 60 for the EU entity if required, but that will need approval from Finance; Ben is on copy to confirm.
- VAT / tax: Redwood invoices the legal entity providing the PO. For EU entities we typically issue a commercial invoice and expect local VAT self-assessment or reverse-charge (we do not gross up). Kimberly, please confirm legal language around invoicing entity/responsibility.
- Minimum commit ramp: We are open to a 40% Q1 ramp with a documented ramp schedule in the Order Form and an activation milestone clause. That should be captured as a milestone-based tranche in the payment schedule.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to provide legal redlines on withholding, tax indemnity, and invoice entity mapping.

3) I’ll return an annotated Order Form (attached) showing the payment split and PO flow.

Alex / team — I reviewed the attached Order Form and flagged a few commercial/legal items. High-level summary below; redline file attached.

1) Invoice / entity mapping: We need a firm billing entity clause (Section 2.1) that states the Redwood legal entity to invoice (Redwood Inference, Inc.) unless Hearthline provides an alternate PO remit-to. If they want the EU BV to be invoiced, we require local tax evidence (VAT registration + invoice remit-to) and a signed SOW specifying that entity.

2) Withholding & gross-up: We cannot accept unlimited gross-up. Proposed compromise: customer is responsible for any withholding taxes; Redwood will provide gross-up only up to a capped amount tied to the initial tranche (cap = 2% of invoice) or allow netting via a credit note mechanism. This avoids unbounded exposure.

3) Net terms exceptions: We can approve Net 60 for EUR entities where local cashflow requirements exist, but approvals must come from Finance (Ben) and require a committed billing entity and PO mapping. Otherwise default Net 45 stands.

4) VAT / reverse charge: Add a customer representation that it will self-assess VAT under reverse-charge where applicable and provide Redwood with necessary VAT IDs and evidence within 10 business days of the first invoice.

5) Minimum commit ramp / milestone: Capture the 40% Q1 ramp as a milestone schedule (Appendix A) with clear activation acceptance criteria; failure to achieve ramp should revert service credits, not immediate termination.

Please review redlines_annotated.docx (attached). I also created a DocuSign envelope placeholder (https://docusign.com/link/hl-ds-4729-final) so we can expedite once approvals are in.
